title: EDA Analysis: Preprocessing, Decomposition, and SCR Detection
text: PhysioEDA provides complete pipeline electrodermal activity (EDA) signal analysis built PhysioExperiment data model. vignette walks core analysis workflow: generating loading EDA data, preprocessing (filtering, artifact correction), tonic/phasic decomposition, SCR peak detection, feature extraction. EDA, also known galvanic skin response (GSR), reflects sympathetic nervous system arousal changes skin conductance. signal can separated slowly varying tonic component (skin conductance level, SCL) rapid phasic responses (skin conductance responses, SCR).

title: EDA Analysis: Preprocessing, Decomposition, and SCR Detection
text: PhysioEDA provides convenience functions generating simulated EDA data. real data, use /O functions PhysioIO.
code: library(PhysioEDA)  # Generate a simulated EDA signal (10 minutes at 10 Hz, 1 channel) x <- make_eda(n_time = 6000, n_channels = 1, sr = 10) x  # Generate EDA with embedded stimulus events x_event <- make_eda_with_scr(n_time = 6000, sr = 10, n_events = 4)

title: EDA Analysis: Preprocessing, Decomposition, and SCR Detection
text: processing, important check signal quality. edaQuality() function computes metrics including flatline detection, artifact percentage, signal--noise ratio, overall quality score. quality score ranges 0 100. Signals scored “good” (>= 70) can proceed directly analysis, “acceptable” (>= 40) signals may benefit artifact correction. “Poor” signals (< 40) examined manually.
code: quality <- edaQuality(x) quality

title: EDA Analysis: Preprocessing, Decomposition, and SCR Detection
text: EDA signals typically lowpass filtered remove high-frequency noise. edaFilter() function uses FFT-based filtering smooth frequency-domain transitions.
code: # Lowpass filter at 1 Hz to remove high-frequency noise x <- edaFilter(x, type = "lowpass", cutoff = 1.0)  # The filtered signal is stored in a new assay SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(x)

title: EDA Analysis: Preprocessing, Decomposition, and SCR Detection

text: edaArtifact() function detects artifacts using threshold, gradient, flatline methods, can correct via linear interpolation.

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: Event-related skin conductance response (ER-SCR) analysis examines phasic EDA changes time-locked experimental events (e.g., stimulus presentations, decisions, feedback). common paradigm psychophysiology research using EDA. vignette demonstrates use PhysioEDA perform event-related SCR analysis, data preparation statistical summary event-locked responses.

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: typical event-related SCR analysis pipeline consists : Load simulate EDA data event markers Preprocess signal (filter, artifact correction) Decompose tonic phasic components Extract event-related SCR features Summarize analyze results

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: edaErscr() function core event-related analysis. event, searches SCR onset within specified latency window extracts amplitude, latency, rise time, 50% recovery time.

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: onset_window: valid latency range (seconds) event onset SCR onset must occur considered event-related. default c(1, 4) reflects typical 1-4 second latency sympathetic responses. peak_window: minimum maximum time SCR onset peak (default: c(0.5, 5)). amplitude_min: minimum amplitude threshold valid SCR (default: 0.01 microsiemens).
code: # Extract event-related SCRs er_results <- edaErscr(x,   event_type = "stimulus",   onset_window = c(1, 4),   peak_window = c(0.5, 5),   amplitude_min = 0.01 )  er_results

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: computing mean amplitudes, common approach include trials valid SCR (responders-) set non-responder amplitudes zero.
code: # Responders-only mean amplitude responders <- er_results[er_results$scr_present, ] if (nrow(responders) > 0) {   mean_amp <- mean(responders$scr_amplitude, na.rm = TRUE)   cat("Mean SCR amplitude (responders):", round(mean_amp, 3), "uS\n") }  # All-trials mean (non-responders = 0) er_results$amplitude_zero <- ifelse(er_results$scr_present,                                      er_results$scr_amplitude, 0) mean_amp_all <- mean(er_results$amplitude_zero) cat("Mean SCR amplitude (all trials):", round(mean_amp_all, 3), "uS\n")

title: Event-Related SCR Analysis
text: events different types values, can compare SCR features across conditions.
code: # If events have different types, filter by event type # Example: comparing CS+ vs CS- in a conditioning paradigm  # Get event metadata events <- getEvents(x) event_df <- events@events  # Merge event metadata with ER-SCR results er_results$event_value <- event_df$value[er_results$event_index]  # Compare conditions (using base R) by_condition <- split(er_results, er_results$event_value) condition_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(by_condition), function(cond) {   d <- by_condition[[cond]]   data.frame(     condition = cond,     n_trials = nrow(d),     response_rate = mean(d$scr_present),     mean_amplitude = mean(d$scr_amplitude, na.rm = TRUE),     mean_latency = mean(d$scr_latency, na.rm = TRUE),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) })) condition_summary

title: Decompose EDA into Tonic and Phasic Components — edaDecompose
text: Five methods available: highpass FFT-based highpass/lowpass separation cutoff frequency. median Sliding median filter tonic extraction. cda Continuous Decomposition Analysis (Benedek & Kaernbach, 2010). Deconvolution Bateman impulse response, Gaussian smoothing, non-negativity constraint driver signal; optional tau2 optimisation. dda Discrete Decomposition Analysis (Benedek & Kaernbach, 2010): continuous CDA driver reduced sparse impulse train (one impulse per significant SCR) reconvolved. cvxeda Exact convex optimization decomposition (Greco et al., 2016), solved quadratic program: cubic-knot spline tonic basis sparse, non-negative sudomotor driver biexponential system, L1 sparsity driver L2 smoothness tonic. Requires quadprog solver; degrades gracefully Wiener approximation unavailable. cvxeda_fast Fast Wiener/ADMM approximation cvxEDA (solver dependency); original iterative approximation.

title: Skin-Conductance Response Function (SCRF) — scrf
text: First-class canonical skin-conductance response kernel used throughout PhysioEDA single source SCR shape (simulation, CDA / cvxEDA deconvolution, GLM designs). response biexponential (Bateman) function h(t) = exp(-t / tau2) - exp(-t / tau1) t >= 0 (0 otherwise), optionally augmented Gaussian bump PsPM-style canonical form (Bach et al., 2010). kernel first/second time-derivatives available (derivatives drive GLM temporal/dispersion regressors).

code: scrf(   t,   tau1 = 0.75,   tau2 = 2,   form = c("bateman", "pspm_canonical"),   normalize = c("peak", "area", "none"),   deriv = 0,   bump_amp = 0.3,   bump_center = NULL,   bump_sd = 0.7 )

title: Skin-Conductance Response Function (SCRF) — scrf
text: t Numeric vector times seconds. Values < 0 return 0. tau1 SCR rise time constant seconds (default: 0.75). tau2 SCR decay time constant seconds (default: 2.0). Must differ tau1; canonical shape tau2 > tau1. form Kernel family: "bateman" (pure biexponential) "pspm_canonical" (biexponential plus Gaussian bump). normalize Normalisation kernel: "peak" (unit maximum, default), "area" (unit integral), "none" (raw). Derivatives scaled constant. deriv Derivative order return: 0 (kernel), 1, 2. bump_amp Gaussian bump amplitude, relative raw Bateman peak, form = "pspm_canonical" (default: 0.3; ignored otherwise). bump_center Gaussian bump centre seconds (default: analytic Bateman peak time). bump_sd Gaussian bump standard deviation seconds (default: 0.7).

title: PhysioEDA 0.2.0
text: Initial release PhysioEDA standalone package x-biosignal ecosystem, split PhysioExperiment monorepo. Provides complete electrodermal activity (EDA / skin conductance) analysis pipeline PhysioExperiment objects, preprocessing tonic/phasic decomposition, SCR detection, feature extraction, visualization.

title: PhysioEDA 0.2.0
text: edaFilter() applies FFT-based lowpass, highpass, bandpass filtering smooth frequency-domain transition. edaDownsample() decimates signal anti-aliasing lowpass stage, preserving events channel metadata. edaArtifact() detects artifacts via threshold, gradient, flatline methods, optional correction linear interpolation NA replacement per-channel, per-method artifact summary. edaQuality() reports per-channel quality metrics (statistics, flatline artifact percentages, Donoho-estimator SNR) overall quality score label. edaDecompose() separates skin conductance tonic (SCL) phasic (SCR) components via four methods: FFT highpass, sliding median, Continuous Decomposition Analysis (cda, Benedek & Kaernbach 2010), convex optimization (cvxeda, Greco et al. 2016). CDA cvxEDA also return sudomotor nerve driver signal. edaPeaks() detects SCR peaks gradient zero-crossing amplitude threshold, reporting onset, peak, amplitude, rise time, 50% recovery time per response. edaFeatures() summarizes per-channel SCR SCL features including SCR count rate, mean amplitude, tonic level, phasic AUC, non-specific SCR count frequency. edaErscr() performs event-related SCR analysis, extracting amplitude, latency, rise time, recovery time time-locked experimental events. edaTransform() edaUntransform() apply invert log, sqrt, zscore, range transformations, storing parameters metadata exact reversal. edaSimulate() generates synthetic EDA known tonic phasic components using Bateman-shaped SCRs. make_eda() make_eda_with_scr() provide ready-made simulated objects (latter stimulus events) testing examples. plotEda(), plotDecompose(), plotPeaks() render base-R plots EDA time series, tonic/phasic/driver decomposition, annotated SCR onsets peaks.
